text: Jaeha asked for two minutes. His plan: husks plug the passage, everyone runs the drain pipe, and one odd note. Fire means flood.
Moon Ahin's husks hold ninety seconds, then follow. Her husks don't retreat, she says. Tonight they learn. He'd like them back.
Thirty-six husks lock into a porcelain wall, four deep, as the guards charge.
Shock batons crackle. The wall doesn't budge.
Everyone else drops onto the drain pipe below: rushing seawater, fifty metres above the pit floor.
Ho skids toward the edge. Jaeha grabs him, and Woo grabs Jaeha.
Uncle Pyo, over Borro's shoulder, insists he can walk. He can't. Carry on, big one.
Stay in the middle, Jaeha shouts. Don't stop for anything.
Across the pit, the freight elevator drops fast: a squad in armour, and one slim figure with a crossbow.
Han Sora steps off like she owns the place, in Kanghan grey now, twelve troopers fanning out behind her.
Her core compass swings toward the pipe. There you are, Operator. She told the Director he'd come.
Then she spots Lyra. The pretty archer from the stream? The Director wants her too, darling.
Moon Ahin orders them all to stand down. She is Moon Ahin.
Sora almost pities her. Director Baek says Miss Moon is asleep at home, so whoever this is, she's trespassing. Fire.
Moon Ahin goes white. The Director has already decided.
Stun bolts fly. Borro and Lyra flare into field form, full fighting strength, and Borro shields Moon Ahin from the volley.
Jaeha carries them both, taking part of every hit into himself. His shoulder bleeds again.
Borro doesn't look round. Stay behind me. The Operator said everyone comes back.
Nib drops among the troopers in field form, but nobody carries him.
Jaeha can only carry two. Every cut Nib takes, he keeps.
Lyra draws her white longbow to full, her braid lifting in the heat from the pit.
Two archers, two styles. Arrow and bolt meet in mid-air and burst apart.
Sora's next bolt pins Lyra's sleeve to the rock. Pretty bow, Sora calls. Slow hands.
Lyra tears free and nocks two arrows at once. Pretty face. Cheap toy.
Two carbines go flying. Sora ducks a third arrow and comes up laughing.
A stun bolt hits Nib. His outline flickers like a dying bulb, and a baton rises over him.
Jaeha switches his CARRY from Lyra to Nib. The next blow lands in Jaeha, and Nib slips free.
But below them, the squad's wall of shields is outrunning the team to the hatch.
Pinned down, Jaeha spots a red panel: a flame, an arrow, a wave. Core tanks burn, so each section floods when it catches fire.
Sprinklers overhead. Bulkhead doors at both ends.
One arrow into the tanks behind the squad, he tells Lyra. A fire, in here? Trust their fire safety. They're very careful people.
The arrow cracks a tank, and violet fire climbs the rack.
A horn, and a calm voice: fire in section 4-C, flooding in five seconds.
The captain orders his men off the catwalk. Sora looks up, delighted. Oh, clever boy.
The doors slam, the section floods, and the fire dies in steam. The squad is swept away, Nib leaps clear, and Sora dangles from the elevator, soaked and laughing.
She climbs up, slicks her wet hair back and concedes. That one, she'll give him.
Back at the balcony, the husk wall finally shatters.
Moon Ahin draws her baton back toward herself, a gesture she has never made. Come back to me, all of you.
The pipe runs past the Tide Warden's chained left arm: a cliff of coral, its cuff as big as a house.
Her husks catch up, two by two. Thirty. They broke six, and her husks held.
She looks almost proud, and doesn't hide it fast enough.
Borro strains at a huge drain hatch, as the speakers send all security to the drain tunnels.
It swings open. A dark, dripping tunnel. The way out.
Then the water in the pipe trembles, and all three summons stop dead.
The Warden's eye opens: deep sea-green, ancient, and fully aware.
His huge head turns in its chains to look down at the three summons.
To Jaeha and Moon Ahin, it's only a deep hum shaking the pipe. Jaeha yells for Nib: what is that?
But the summons hear words in their own language. Child of the Ninth Wall. Child of the River. Child of the Stone.
Lyra is crying, her lips moving as if she knows the words.
Four years he has sung into the water, and no one from home has answered.
Nib kneels in the water, fist on chest, the salute of the Ninth Wall. Borro bows his head.
Jaeha asks what he said. Four years of singing, Nib tells him. Nobody came. Now they're here.
Behind them, torch beams bob closer down the pipe.
Then the eye turns to Jaeha and narrows, and the hum goes deeper.
Nib translates. Jaeha carries their pain, so the Warden wants him to hear his.
Everyone looks from the eye to Jaeha.
He pulls off his respirator and looks up, bare-faced. He's listening. What does the Warden want?
Far below, the chained hand slowly opens, palm up.
And the hero Kanghan has farmed for four years makes his plea. End me, or free me. One or the other. Only do not leave me here.
